The two function definitions (`build()` and `package()`) are parsed but never invoked during this command, so their contents (patching, cmake, make install) cannot execute at this stage.

No suspicious patterns are present: there is no `eval`, no command substitution (`$(...)` or backticks), no `curl`/`wget`, no base64 decoding, no obfuscation, and no attempt to reach an unrelated or unexpected network host. Both source URLs resolve to the package's own upstream GitHub repository (`grizzlypeak3d/tlRender`), which is expected for this package. The `sha256sums` are real 64-character hex digests, not SKIP entries. The `subprocessh-git` dependency is simply a dependency-list string using the AUR convention of appending `-git` to denote a git-tracking package — it is not executed during sourcing.

In short, sourcing this PKGBUILD for `--printsrcinfo` performs no network I/O, writes no files, and executes no payload. The gate is safe; full-function auditing of `build()`/`package()` belongs to the later comprehensive review.
</details>
